name: Magnesium glycinate
lead: Magnesium glycinate, also called magnesium bisglycinate or diglycinate, is the magnesium salt of glycine, containing about 14.1 percent elemental magnesium by mass [1]. It is sold as a supplement to relieve magnesium deficiency and also appears in cosmetics [1]. Marketing often presents it as better tolerated and more absorbable than magnesium oxide, and it is popular for sleep, relaxation and recovery [2].

Glycine, the amino acid in the chelate, functions as an inhibitory neurotransmitter in the spinal cord and brainstem and acts as a co-agonist at NMDA receptors, which proponents cite as a reason the glycinate form is seen as calming [11]. Wikipedia does not address absorption, evidence or adverse effects of the salt itself [1]. Human studies comparing magnesium compounds exist, but trials specifically on glycinate for sleep or appearance are limited.

paras: Magnesium glycinate has the formula C4H8MgN2O4 and a molar mass of about 172.4 g/mol; its systematic name is magnesium bis(aminoacetate) [1]. It is often sold buffered with magnesium oxide, and a pure unbuffered form is also available [1]. It is used in dietary supplements to relieve deficiency and in cosmetics [1].

The main stated use is addressing or preventing magnesium deficiency [1]. Reference text also lists proposed uses for sleep quality, anxiety, muscle soreness and migraines, which is a description of claims rather than established findings [2].
A 2019 study investigated dose-dependent absorption of different magnesium compounds [3]. The article is a comparison of compounds; specific glycinate results are not summarised here.

Soluble magnesium salts such as chloride, citrate and sulfate are absorbed at roughly 30-40 percent, oxide and hydroxide forms less efficiently, and amino-acid chelates such as glycinate and lysinate are described as better tolerated [12]. Diarrhoea is the most common symptom of excess oral magnesium, and healthy kidneys excrete the surplus [12]. Deficiency, most often linked to diuretics, long-term proton pump inhibitors, alcohol use and malabsorption disorders, is reported in about 3-10 percent of the general population [13]. A T Nation forum poster writes that glycinate is probably the form to choose if using only one; this is a user opinion [14].

Randomised trials of combined magnesium and vitamin D supplementation have examined vitamin D status, inflammation and blood pressure, and separately bone turnover and glycaemic control (the latter reporting no influence) [4][5]. Newer reports include a randomised study of glycinate as add-on therapy in hypomagnesaemic asthma and COPD, and a case report of high-dose glycinate in severe hypomagnesaemia [6]. A rat study examined chronic glycinate effects on intestinal motility [7]. Registered trials examine magnesium for insomnia [8] and in athletes for sleep and recovery [9], with no published outcomes in these sources.
Reference text states diarrhoea is the main reported effect, described as less frequent than with other magnesium forms, and severe renal impairment is listed as a contraindication [2].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org magnesium glycinate appears in sleep-supplement stacks.

claims.claim: Magnesium glycinate stacked with L-theanine and GABA improves or lengthens sleep
claims.believers: A looksmax.org user reported sleeping from 1 am to 4 pm after taking the combination and described it as useful for sleep [10].
claims.experts: A registered trial is comparing magnesium with a melatonin congener in primary insomnia; no outcome from a glycinate-specific sleep trial is cited here [8].

claims.claim: Glycinate is the best-tolerated form of magnesium
claims.believers: A T Nation poster says glycinate is the form to choose if sticking to one [14].
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes amino-acid chelates such as glycinate as better tolerated, and a systematic review found organic forms generally more bioavailable than inorganic ones [12]; direct head-to-head trials of tolerability are limited.

card.summary: A glycine-bound magnesium supplement popular for sleep and calm; the claims outrun the glycinate-specific trials.
card.note: Severe kidney impairment is listed as a contraindication.

quick.overview:
Magnesium glycinate is magnesium bound to glycine, sold to address deficiency and popular for sleep and relaxation. It is about 14 percent elemental magnesium.

Marketing says it is gentler and better absorbed than oxide forms; glycinate-specific trials for sleep are few.
quick.mechanism: It supplies magnesium, a mineral involved in many enzyme and nerve functions, with glycine, which proponents say adds a calming effect.
quick.risks: Diarrhoea is the main reported effect, described as milder than with other forms. Severe renal impairment is listed as a contraindication in reference text.

chain: Magnesium glycinate is taken orally, often in the evening
Users report calmer sleep and relaxed muscles
Steadier sleep and recovery are said to support consistent training
angle.text: People use magnesium glycinate in sleep and recovery routines, linking restful sleep and relaxed muscles to training consistency and physique.
